source_text:
βούλεται δὲ εἰπεῖν, ὅτι τοῖς νῦν πρῶτον
προσϊοῦσι τῇ πίστει τὴν περὶ τούτων διδασκαλίαν οἱονεὶ θεμέλιον
προκαταβαλλόμεθα, μετανοεῖν μὲν ἀπὸ τῶν νεκροποιῶν ἔργων εἰκότως πρῶτον
αὐτοὺς προτρεπόμενοι, μετανοοῦντας δὲ πιστεύειν ἐπὶ θεόν, πιστεύοντας δὲ

βαπτίζεσθαι, βαπτιζομένους δὲ τῇ τῶν ἱερατικῶν χειρῶν ὑποταγῆναι αὐτοὺς
ἐπιθέσει πρὸς μετουσίαν τοῦ πνεύματος, τούτου δὲ μετασχόντας περὶ τῆς ἐκ νεκρῶν
ἀναστάσεως μηκέτι διαπιστεῖν, ἀναστησομένους δὲ καὶ αὖθις ἀναβιωσομένους
ἔσεσθαι κρίσιν εἰδέναι, καὶ 422 διηνεκῆ καὶ δικαίαν καὶ ὧν ἐνταῦθα βεβιώκαμεν τὴν
ἀντίδοσιν περιμένειν.
{Hebr. 9,2} Καθ' ἕνα μὲν οὖν λόγον οἶμαι τὴν μὲν λυχνίαν, ὡς εἴρηται, τὸ ἐκ
τῶν αἰσθητῶν τούτων ἀστέρων αἰνίττεσθαι φῶς, τὴν τράπεζαν δὲ τὴν γῆν, τὴν δὲ
πρόθεσιν τῶν ἄρτων τὴν ἐκ τῆς γῆς τῶν ἡμῖν ἐπιτηδείων ἀνάδοσιν.
thought_title: The foundation of teaching and the tabernacle symbols
orientation: The author is explaining Hebrews 6:1, laying out the sequence of foundational Christian teaching, then turning to the symbolism of the tabernacle furnishings from Hebrews 9:2.
pass_a_gloss: But he wishes to say that for those now first approaching the faith we lay down beforehand the teaching about these things as a kind of foundation, first reasonably urging them to repent from the death-dealing works, and when they have repented to believe in God, and when they have believed to be baptized, and when they have been baptized to submit themselves to the laying on of priestly hands for participation in the Spirit, and when they have partaken of this no longer to doubt about the resurrection from the dead, and when they are to rise and live again to know that there will be judgment, and to await the everlasting and just recompense of what we have lived here. And according to one account I think the lampstand, as has been said, hints at the light from these visible stars, and the table hints at the earth, and the presentation of the loaves hints at the earth's yielding up of the things suitable for us.

choices.why: The compound means works that produce death, not merely dead works; the literal force of the -ποιός suffix is preserved.
The compound verb has the prefix προ- indicating prior action, matching the foundation imagery of Hebrews 6:1.

choices.english: to submit themselves to the laying on
choices.why: The middle/passive infinitive with accusative subject keeps the reflexive force of the Greek construction.
rejected: to be subjected to the laying on
to submit to the laying on

choices.why: The verb means to speak in riddles or darkly; 'hints at' preserves the indirect, symbolic sense.
The noun from ἀναδίδωμι means a giving up or producing from below, fitting the earth's provision.

bible_refs.note: The whole passage expands the foundation of teaching from Hebrews 6:1, with the sequence of repentance, faith, baptism, laying on of hands, resurrection, and judgment.
The section heading {Hebr. 9,2} marks the source for the lampstand, table, and presentation of the loaves.

pass_b_english: He wants to say this: for those now first approaching the faith, we lay down beforehand, as it were, a foundation of teaching about these matters. We rightly urge them first to repent from death-dealing works, then, once they have repented, to believe in God; once they believe, to be baptized; once baptized, to submit themselves to the laying on of hands for participation in the Spirit; once they share in this, no longer to doubt the resurrection from the dead; and once they are raised and live again, to know that there will be judgment, and to await the unending and just recompense for how we have lived here.

According to one line of thought, then, I think the lampstand, as has been said, hints at the light from these visible stars, the table hints at the earth, and the bread of the Presence hints at the earth's yielding up of the things suitable for us.
